t: That section 552(a) of title 37, United States Code, is amended by adding the following sentence: “Notwithstanding section 1523 of title 10 or any other provision of law, the promotion of a member while he is in a missing status is fully effective for all purposes, even though the Secretary concerned determines under section 556(b) of this title that the member died before the promotion was made.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Secretary's "determination" implies some decision process with outside input, but the text provides none. The section only makes a missing service member's promotion fully effective even if the Secretary later determines the member died before it was made. No outside party is consulted, no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or advisory body is involved, and no right to sue is granted, so the only actor is a federal official.
fable.s: the promotion of a member while he is in a missing status is fully effective for all purposes, even though the Secretary concerned determines under section 556(b) of this title that the member died before the promotion was made.

qwen_block.w: This section defines the legal effect of a military promotion for a service member who is missing or deceased. It involves internal administrative determinations by a federal official (the Secretary) regarding the status of a federal employee. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation by any party outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in making this decision.
qwen_block.s: Notwithstanding section 1523 of title 10 or any other provision of law, the promotion of a member while he is in a missing status is fully effective for all purposes, even though the Secretary concerned determines under section 556(b) of this title that the member died before the promotion was made.

opus.w: This provision only states that a promotion made while a service member is missing stays fully valid, even if the Secretary later decides the member had already died. The Secretary's decision is internal to the federal government. It involves no outside parties, public comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking or right to sue. Mentioning a Secretary's 'determination' is not participation.
opus.s: the promotion of a member while he is in a missing status is fully effective for all purposes, even though the Secretary concerned determines under section 556(b) of this title that the member died before the promotion was made.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** One could misread this as participation because it mentions a decision made by "the Secretary concerned" under section 556(b). But that decision is a purely internal military finding about whether a member died, and no one outside the federal government is consulted. The provision only says that a promotion granted while a member is missing stays fully valid. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

2. **Answer.**

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the legal status of a military promotion when a member is missing or deceased. It involves an internal determination by a federal official (the Secretary) regarding the timing of death relative to promotion. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation by any party outside the federal government (such as family members, states, or the public) in making this determination.
qwen_chat.s: Notwithstanding section 1523 of title 10 or any other provision of law, the promotion of a member while he is in a missing status is fully effective for all purposes, even though the Secretary concerned determines under section 556(b) of this title that the member died before the promotion was made.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary's determination involves some form of consultation or hearing with the family or the member, but the text only describes the legal effect of a promotion and the Secretary's internal determination of death. It does not mandate any interaction with outside parties.
